items.title: Spot the Machiya
items.task: Find a house that is skinny on the street and seems to go far back.
items.reveal: Machiya are townhouses: a small face, a long body.

moreInfo.title: The front
moreInfo.text: People often say a narrow front paid less tax. Treat that as a story to check, not a fact, until a source is attached.

items.notes: Do not teach the tax story as certain.

items.title: Maiko or Tourist?
items.task: If you see someone in geiko or maiko dress, do not chase them for a photo. Watch from a distance. Ask: working person, or visitor in costume?
items.reveal: This is a workplace. Respect beats a picture.

moreInfo.title: How to look
moreInfo.text: Do not block the street. Do not touch. Do not follow. A posed tourist in rented clothes is not a hunt target either.

items.notes: Ethics mission. Not a scavenger hunt for working geiko/maiko.

items.title: Why Gion Exists Here
items.task: Stand near Yasaka and look toward the lanes of food and inns. Who was this street for?
items.reveal: Shrine visitors needed food, beds and shows. Gion grew to serve them.
items.notes: Confirm shrine visitors, lodging and entertainment without inventing a founding myth.
